mcp.title: Model Context Protocol
mcp.subtitle: Connect AI coding assistants to Aexy

overview.heading: Overview
overview.descriptionAfter: lets AI assistants like Claude Code, Claude Desktop and OpenAI Codex interact directly with your Aexy workspace — managing sprints, querying analytics, running agents, and more through natural language.
overview.summary: {total} operations across {categories} capabilities, generated from the backend's own API schema. What you are offered is filtered to the apps you hold.

step1.title: Create an API token
step1.description: For a remote connection nothing is needed — you sign in when the client asks. For a local (stdio) bridge, create a token; it authenticates as you and carries only your permissions.

step2.title: Pick your client
step2.description: Remote clients connect straight to the server URL. Local clients run the aexy-mcp bridge through uvx, so there is nothing to clone or keep updated.

step3.title: Add the configuration
step3.description: Copy the block for your client below into the file it names, then restart the client.

clientSetup.heading: Client Setup

intro.claudeCode: One line for the remote server, which authenticates through the browser. Or run the stdio bridge with a token — commit .mcp.json so everyone on the repo gets it.
intro.claudeDesktop: Add the server URL under Settings → Connectors and sign in when asked. Or point the desktop config at the stdio bridge; quit and reopen the app afterwards.
intro.chatgpt: ChatGPT reaches Aexy over HTTP instead of running a local process. In ChatGPT, open Settings → Connectors → Create, paste the URL below, and approve the workspace it asks for.
intro.codex: Codex reads MCP servers from its TOML config. Add this table, then restart Codex.
intro.cursor: Cursor and VS Code use the same stdio server with slightly different file shapes. Use whichever matches your editor.
intro.other: Any client that speaks streamable HTTP can use the URL with OAuth. Any client that launches processes can run the bridge with this shape.

remoteAuth.body: No API token needed. ChatGPT registers itself and sends you here to sign in, where you pick which workspace it may use. It sees exactly the apps you already have access to in that workspace — never more. Review or revoke it any time under Settings → Connected Apps.

env.apiToken: Your API token, created in Settings → API Tokens
env.workspaceId: Which workspace to act in. Needed only if you belong to more than one.

clientSetup.bridgeNote: The bridge holds no tools of its own. Every call goes through the same server, so the tool list, governance and the audit ledger are identical whichever route you take.
